description.text: The effect is applied only to these channels.

Control the influence of the pixel colors during the filtering. If this value is small, only pixels that have very similar colors will be mixed together, thus preserving the edges in the image. If this value is large, pixels having a large color difference will also affect each other, thus resulting in smoother edges and larger areas having non-uniform color.

gaussian filter: color weighted to differences in surrounding pixel color and how close the pixels are to each other.
median filter: pixels are weighted according to the middle value pixel.
Use 4 * (1 - mask) * mask to mix.

This is the GPU that will be used for rendering, when Use GPU if available is selected. If you have more than one GPU in your machine, you can select a different GPU Device to use by editing your Preferences. (Note that selecting a different GPU will require a restart of Nuke to take effect.) Local GPU will be shown as Not available when any of the following is true: * Use CPU is selected as the GPU Device in your Preferences. * No suitable GPU was found on your system. Please refer to the documentation for details of the requirements for GPU acceleration. * It was not possible to create a context for processing on the selected GPU. For example, this can happen when there is not enough free memory available on the GPU. To use the GPU when rendering from the command line, add --gpu to your command.

Channels in the guide image used to compute the filtering weights. The guide image should contain some prior information on the source useful to the filtering. If no information is available, the result of an unguided filtering can be used as guide input of a second filtering operation.

Control the influence of the pixel positions during the filtering. If this value is small, only pixels that are close to each other will be mixed together. If this value is large, distant pixels will also affect each other as long as their colors are similar.
Control the size of the filter.

Select this to render on the Local GPU, if available. You can select this even if no GPU is currently available on your machine. The GPU will then be used whenever the script is opened on a machine which does have a GPU available. You should also select this if you wish to render from the command line with the --gpu option. If this node requires full frames from its inputs, and is therefore unable to reduce its memory overhead, it will fall back to the CPU if an attempt to render a frame on the GPU fails due to lack of memory. When this occurs, a warning message will be printed to the console.

description.plain_text: Bilateral: Applies the bilateral filter to the source image. The bilateral filter operates by mixing nearby source pixels according to both their spatial distance and color similarity. The color similarity can be computed from the optional guide input. If the guide is not given, the output format will be equal to the source format and the node will act as a standard bilateral filter. If the guide is given, the output will have the same format as the guide. If the guide and source formats are equal, the node will act as a cross bilateral filter. Otherwise, if the guide and source formats are different, the node will act as a joint bilateral resampler.
